title: Make Codex worktree startup unattended
description: Follow-up to OnTrack-z2y: Codex startup prompts for workspace trust or available updates prevent Herdr agent startup and prompt delivery. User authorizes automatically trusting the new worktree and skipping update prompts. Use supported scoped Codex startup settings without disabling sandbox/approval protections or changing global configuration; test argv and path escaping, preserve OpenCode behavior, and document limits.
notes:
Official Codex 0.162.1 loader source confirms CLI projects.<main-repository-root>.trust_level="trusted" is merged before trust calculation; linked worktrees resolve main repository root. Plan invocation-only trust + check_for_update_on_startup=false, no global configuration or sandbox/approval changes. API reconciliation is currently running; trust implementation queued after it terminates.
Blocked by confirmed concurrent filesystem writes after user requested reconciliation: src/ui.rs SHA-256 changed 3ffaafa4… -> 3e716482…, size 91001 -> 92071 bytes, mtime 21:45:54 -> 21:47:37 while fixer had not edited it. Latest src/herdr.rs trust/API changes are partial and unvalidated. Stop writers before resuming; no live agents/worktrees or global config mutations performed.
Implemented invocation-only Codex project trust for verified canonical main repository and check_for_update_on_startup=false. No global config writes or sandbox/approval changes; OpenCode unchanged. Reconciled typed UI/backend API preserving full-Bead capture, fixed footer width, bounded agent names to Herdr 32-character limit. Trust review found no scope/escaping/permission issue; subsequent launch blockers fixed and parent inspected corrections. Final fixer gates passed: cargo fmt --check; cargo test (143 passed); cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings; cargo build; git diff --check. Live Codex startup not exercised. Source launches require main checkout; linked/nested/redirected source Git layouts reject before creation with guidance. Auth/admin policy/unknown prompts may still require intervention. Changes uncommitted; no push/sync.
close_reason: Codex launches now receive verified repository-scoped trust and update suppression per invocation, with regression coverage and all quality gates passing.

title: Integrate herdr functionality
description: This application should work in tandem with the herdr multiplexer. Once a Bead has been defined, add the ability to send it off to a herdr worktree under the current running workspace and pass it to an agent harness such as Opencode or Codex. Discover which agents are currently available through herdr's integration functionality.
notes: Implementation lanes: isolated src/herdr.rs CLI adapter + app/UI async handoff dialog. Preserve pre-existing navigation/detail styling edits. Verified local Herdr 0.9.1 and running server; integration status exposes installed Codex/OpenCode/Hermes. Evidence plan: injected command executor tests for discovery/create/start/prompt success, malformed output and partial-failure recovery; channel-driven app tests for captured selection, stale response suppression and duplicate submission guards; Ratatui TestBackend tests for normal/compact dialog and all agent choices. Baseline 106 tests passed. Final required gates: cargo fmt --check, cargo test, cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings, cargo build. No real worktree creation or agent launch during validation; live end-to-end remains an explicitly reported limit.
close_reason: Implemented Herdr worktree/agent handoff with explicit confirmation, regression coverage, documentation, passing full quality gates, and resolved independent safety review.

title: Run in-progress task in the background
description: Currently, when a task is started a window pops up and locks us until the task completes. Once started, tasks should start autonomously in the background, with the application keeping track of the ongoing status. This will allow us to run multiple tasks in parallel
acceptance_criteria:
Inferred acceptance criteria (execution entry point requires clarification):
1. Starting an executable task returns control to the application without a modal that waits for task completion.
2. Two distinct tasks can remain in progress concurrently; starting the second does not wait for the first.
3. The application tracks each launched task independently and exposes its ongoing status, completion, and failure without blocking navigation or refresh.
4. Repeated starts of an already-running task do not accidentally launch duplicate work.
5. Automated tests cover concurrent starts, responsiveness, independent completion/failure, and duplicate prevention; existing terminal cleanup and browsing behavior remain intact.
6. User and developer documentation explains starting tasks, status tracking, and the chosen lifecycle behavior.
notes:
Scope inference and assumptions (2026-10-14): The existing description is preserved. This worktree currently implements a Rust Beads browser with create/delete mutations; src/app.rs has a single background worker for bd calls and src/ui.rs has create/delete/settings dialogs. Neither the README nor the execution paths expose a task-start command or agent runner. Assume “task” means executing work on a selected Bead, not merely a create/delete mutation, because the original description explicitly requests parallel in-progress tasks. No implementation has begun.
Open questions: Is the intended task-start implementation missing from this worktree, should a new agent-launch integration be added (which runner/command?), or does the request actually refer to the existing create/delete dialogs? The runner choice and whether launched work survives application exit cannot safely be inferred. Acceptance criteria are inferred behavior targets; implementation is blocked pending clarification of the execution entry point.

title: Enrich title-only tasks during agent handoff
description: When an OnTrack task has only a title, instruct the dispatched agent to infer a reasonable actionable description and acceptance criteria from the title and available project context, save those requirements to the live Bead before implementation, and avoid refusing solely because description or acceptance criteria are missing. Preserve existing requirements and make assumptions explicit; seek clarification only for consequential ambiguity that cannot be reasonably resolved.
close_reason: Updated agent handoff to infer and persist missing requirements before implementation; regression coverage added. cargo fmt --check, all 144 tests, clippy -D warnings, and build pass. External agent compliance remains outside prompt-test coverage.

title: Ping
notes:
Assumptions inferred from the title-only live issue and repository context: Ping means an executable liveness probe exposed as --ping, with the conventional pong response. It does not check network connectivity or Beads database health. Scope is a single exact --ping argument; other invocations preserve existing behavior. No existing nonempty description or acceptance criteria were present.
Implemented the documented --ping interpretation. Validation passed: cargo fmt --check; cargo test (102 passed); cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings; cargo build; git diff --check. Built-binary check in an isolated temporary directory with empty PATH, isolated HOME/config, and redirected streams returned exit 0, exact pong newline, empty stderr, and created no files. No-argument PTY smoke check entered/exited alternate screen, quit with q at exit 0, and restored terminal attributes. Updated src/main.rs, README.md, docs/user-guide.md, docs/development.md; synchronized CLAUDE.md with AGENTS.md per repository invariant.
User requested reverting this implementation. The inferred --ping scope and acceptance criteria are withdrawn and cleared; original title Ping remains. Issue reopened pending user-defined scope. Implementation commit 0968b1d reverted.

title: Skip group headers during Bead selection
description: Remove selectable task group headers. Up from first item moves to previous group's last item; Down from last item moves to next group's first item. Preserve sensible outer-boundary and collapse behavior, test navigation and refresh edge cases, and update docs.
notes: User refinement: collapsed group headers must be keyboard selectable for reopening. Skip only expanded headers; preserve direct item-to-item navigation between expanded groups.
close_reason: Collapsed headers selectable via keyboard and reopen with Right/Space; expanded headers skipped. Navigation, refresh, identity and rendering regression coverage passes. All 106 tests, fmt, clippy, build and diff check passed.
